answer: Because the juniper ordering is published with the oasis batch, the horizon audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. A farm that floods the queue early thus gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 24% of the queue is processed in arrival order. A 112 account operation therefore ties up 15 million dollars of idle capital. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
